body_html:
Moc Chau, a high plateau in Son La province, sits roughly 180 to 200 km from Hanoi along National Highway 6. This guide sets out what the sources reviewed say about the distance, the route and what a press travel guide advises motorbike riders, then the seasons, the crowds in blossom time and a two-day outline. It also lists what the sources do not cover: current road works or closures, fuel stops, parking and the rules on which roads a motorbike may use.

Distance and route from Hanoi

The figures disagree a little, so the table keeps them apart rather than blending them.

FigureSource and date
About 180 km from Hanoi, 120 km from Son La CityViet Nam National Authority of Tourism feature, 17 March 2021
About 200 km from HanoiVietnam Tourism (vietnam.travel); the page shows no date but mentions the 2022 World Travel Awards
Almost 200 km, about 4 hours by carVnExpress guide, published 15 May 2020, updated 12 January 2026
About 4 to 5 hours by motorbikeVnExpress guide, same dates

Treat the distance as 180 to 200 km. The 2021 authority feature traces the way as National Highway 6 from Hanoi through Hoa Binh city, over the Cun, Moi and Thung Khe passes and on up to the plateau at about 1,000 m. The sources do not give turn-by-turn directions, and none says which roads a motorbike may use, for example whether any expressway section on the way is open to motorbikes. Confirm that with the local authority before planning the route.

Riding it on a motorbike

For riders, VnExpress recommends the old Highway 6 because of the scenery along it, but warns that the surface is quite degraded in places and tells riders to take care with their steering. It gives 4 to 5 hours for the ride. The guide was first published in 2020 and updated in January 2026, so both the road remark and the time estimate may be out of date. None of the sources defines the old Highway 6 on a map or reports current road works, so no bypass is named here.

A few other points from the same guide are worth planning around:

  • A popular stop is an S-shaped bend in Van Ho district, where, the guide says, most riders pause for the view and photographs.
  • In summer there is less fog, though rain limits visibility. The stretch most likely to be misty begins at Thung Khe.
  • Days are usually warm but nights are cold and misty. The guide advises bringing warm clothes and checking the bike's lights before leaving.

When to go

VnExpress describes the plateau as having something in bloom or in season for much of the year. Its month-by-month account, not an official calendar, runs as follows.

Time of yearWhat the guide lists
JanuaryTea hills with new shoots; peach, plum, apricot and cherry (mai anh đào) blossom
From mid-MayPlums ripening and the harvest
SummerNo flowers, but clean air and outdoor activities
August to DecemberPersimmons; the crisp variety usually comes first, from August to October
NovemberWhite mustard flowers begin
DecemberWild sunflowers colour the plateau

Vietnam Tourism (vietnam.travel) also lists apricot, plum and peach blossoms, without months.

Blossom weeks: crowds and prices

Plum blossom after Tet is a very busy period. The Vietnam News Agency's policy-and-life site, in a report published around February 2025, said the 2025 plum bloom came after the Tet holiday; because some gardens flowered early and others late, plum-blossom tourism stretched to about five or six weeks instead of one or two weeks of full bloom. It adds that garden owners time the stripping of leaves so trees flower when visitors arrive. No source gives official bloom dates for 2026 or 2027, and the bloom depends on weather and on each garden.

The same report described rooms, food and entertainment services and traffic as overloaded, and a homestay owner quoted in the report said most rooms were booked from the second day of Tet to the end of February. It quoted garden entry at 20,000 to 50,000 VND per person and motorbike-taxi rides to the higher gardens at 50,000 to 150,000 VND per person per trip, depending on the area. These are 2025 press figures and only indicative. The VnExpress guide quotes guesthouse rooms at about 200,000 to 300,000 VND a night and homestays at 300,000 to 1,000,000 VND, but it dates from 2020 (updated 2026) and these figures say nothing about blossom-week rates. No source gives sight opening hours.

A two-day outline

VnExpress says Moc Chau can be covered quickly in 2 days, with 3 to 4 days better. On the guide's own estimate the ride takes 4 to 5 hours each way, so a weekend trip spends roughly 8 to 10 hours in the saddle. With cold, misty nights and fog most likely from Thung Khe, it makes sense to aim to arrive in daylight.

The plateau is about 80 km long and 25 km wide, and more than 1,000 m above sea level, so sights are spread out. Vietnam Tourism (vietnam.travel) describes about 3,000 hectares of tea fields, the largest tea-growing area in Vietnam, and notes that bicycle and motorbike rentals are available there; it gives no providers or prices. Its headline sights include Dai Yem waterfall, which has two shelves and a drop of over 100 m from the top, and Pha Luong Peak at about 2,000 m, which it says takes quite a bit of uphill hiking to reach. An illustrative split is day one for the ride up and whatever daylight remains for the tea hills, then day two for the waterfall and the ride back. The sources give a few distances from Moc Chau town (about 5 km to Dai Yem per the 2021 TITC feature; 30 km to Pha Luong Peak, plus a 3- to 4-hour walk from the border post, per VnExpress) but none between sights, so check locally.

If a ride of that length is too much for one weekend, closer options from Hanoi include Duong Lam from Hanoi by Motorbike: Village Access and a Day-Trip Plan and Soc Son from Hanoi by Motorbike: A Day Plan With a Weather Backup. For a wider plan that stays in the Hanoi area, see Three Days in Hanoi With a Rental Motorbike: Plan Distinct Routes.

What to confirm before you ride

  • Road condition. Look for current news on Highway 6, including works, landslides and closures. The sources report none and are not current on this point.
  • Roads open to motorbikes. Ask the local authority which roads on the way are open to motorbikes.
  • Taking the bike this far. Ask the rental shop whether the bike may go on a trip of 180 to 200 km each way, and what to arrange for the return.
  • Fuel and parking. No source covers fuel stops or parking, so plan to check them on the day.
  • Prices and rooms. Garden entry and motorbike-taxi fares quoted above are from 2025; book rooms early if the trip falls in blossom weeks.
  • Weather. Check the forecast for fog and rain on the Thung Khe stretch, and pack warm clothes for the night.

Sources checked

  • Vietnam Tourism (vietnam.travel), Moc Chau feature, undated: distance, tea fields, rentals, waterfall and peak. vietnam.travel Moc Chau page
  • Viet Nam National Authority of Tourism (TITC), feature of 17 March 2021: the 180 km figure and the Highway 6 route. vietnamtourism.gov.vn Moc Chau feature
  • VnExpress travel guide to Moc Chau (published 15 May 2020, updated 12 January 2026): riding advice, fog, seasons by month and trip length. vnexpress.net Moc Chau travel guide
  • Vietnam News Agency policy-and-life site, published around February 2025: the 2025 plum season, crowds and indicative prices. chinhsachcuocsong.vnanet.vn report on the Moc Chau plum season

Thuê xe máy Nguyễn Hà is open 09:00–21:00 daily at Ngõ 5 Nguyễn Văn Cừ, Bồ Đề, Long Biên, Hà Nội (near Gia Lâm bus station). Phone: 0334 699 969.
